facts.fact_text: On 21 August 2003 the non-governmental organisation "City-wide public council for the protection of citizens' rights in town planning and for the protection of the environment" decided to hold an assembly of Krylatskoye district residents at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square in Moscow.
One purpose of the planned assembly was to protest against the Moscow mayor's failure to respond to the resolution of the assembly held in May 2003.
One purpose of the planned assembly was to protest against the planned construction of several luxurious blocks of flats in the place of facilities for sports and children.
One purpose of the planned assembly was to cast a vote of no confidence in the city authorities and call for their resignation.
One purpose of the planned assembly was to discuss matters of local self-governance.
On 4 September 2003 a few dozen residents gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square.
The applicant was among the residents who gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003.
On 3 September 2003 the prefect of the Western Administrative District of Moscow cancelled his previous decision of 29 August 2003 accepting the notice of the planned assembly.
On 3 September 2003 the police were instructed "to take measures to prevent the assembly planned for 4 September 2003 at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square from being held".
The police dispersed the crowd at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003 by force.
According to the administrative-arrest record of 4 September 2003, the applicant was arrested for refusing to comply with a lawful order of the police.
The judge of the Kuntsevskiy District Court fined the applicant 1,000 Russian roubles (approximately 30 euros) on the charge of organising an unauthorised assembly.
The Russian Constitution guarantees the right to freedom of peaceful assembly and the right to hold meetings, demonstrations, marches and pickets under Article 31.
Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 was in force at the material time pursuant to Russian Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992.

Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, organisers of an assembly were required to serve written notice on the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly (§ 2).
Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, the municipal authority was required to give its response no later than five days before the assembly (§ 3).

Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, an assembly could be banned if its purpose was contrary to the Constitution or threatened public order or the security of citizens.
The Suppression of Terrorism Act (Federal Law no. 130-FZ of 25 July 1998) was in force at the material time.

Under the Suppression of Terrorism Act (Federal Law no. 130-FZ of 25 July 1998), the Ministry of the Interior fought terrorism by way of preventing, detecting and putting an end to terrorist offences pursuing lucrative goals (section 7 § 3).

Under the Suppression of Terrorism Act (Federal Law no. 130-FZ of 25 July 1998), regional executive bodies, municipal bodies, public associations and organisations and State officials were required to assist the authorities responsible for suppression of terrorism (section 9 § 1).

The prefect cancelled his decision of 29 August 2003 "in connection with the operative information of law-enforcement authorities about an expected outbreak of terrorist activities in the Krylatskoye district and with a view to ensuring the safety of the district's residents".
On 3 September 2003 the police were instructed "to take measures to prevent the assembly planned for 4 September 2003 at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square from being held".

In the letter of 2 September 2003, the head of the police command of the Western Administrative District asked the prefect to annul his decision of 29 August 2003 because the police command "had received, from various sources, information about potential terrorist attacks in Moscow, in places of mass gatherings".

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that the prefect's decision of 3 September 2003 was issued not in connection with the notice filed by the assembly organisers but in connection with a threat of increasing terrorist activities in the areas of mass gatherings, with a view to ensuring the security of the Krylatskoye District's residents.

The prefect cancelled his decision of 29 August 2003 "in connection with the operative information of law-enforcement authorities about an expected outbreak of terrorist activities in the Krylatskoye district and with a view to ensuring the safety of the district's residents".
On 5, 6 and 7 September 2003 (Friday to Sunday) the "Day of the City" was celebrated throughout Moscow.
The programme for the "Day of the City" festivities had been approved by the Moscow Government's resolution of 12 August 2003.
The programme for the "Day of the City" festivities included sixty-one events.

The "Day of the City" events included the "World-wide Tea Festival", the opening ceremony, "Parade of the Festivals", the European champions' road running cup, the Moscow cup of the automobile all-round competition, the children's artistic and sport performance, sound and light show, students' parade, and many others.
The "Day of the City" events took place in major public thoroughfares.
The applicant submitted media reports showing that no scheduled "Day of the City" events had been cancelled.
The applicant submitted media reports showing that the "Day of the City" public festivities had been attended by thousands of people.
The Kuntsevskiy District Court asked Krylatskoye police station to produce the operative information which had been the basis for cancelling the authorisation for the assembly.
On 16 December 2003 Krylatskoye police station replied that there had been no operative information in their possession.

On 21 January 2004 the police command of the Western Administrative District of Moscow replied that the material requested was classified as secret and for that reason could not be made available to the judge.
In a judgment of 30 January 2004, the Kuntsevskiy District Court rejected the applicant's complaint against the prefect's decision of 3 September 2003.

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that no evidence contradicting the information contained in the letter from the police command of the Western Administrative District to the prefect of the Western Administrative District had been produced before the court.

The applicant submitted on appeal that not a single public gathering organised by the Moscow mayor's office in the framework of the "Day of the City" had been cancelled as a result of a potential terrorist threat.
